_comment: Gates whose failure is KNOWN, JUSTIFIED and deliberately carried past the
push guard. This is not a way to push green CI -- CI still runs every gate
and still fails on anything listed here. It only lets the push HAPPEN, with
the failure named on the record instead of routed around silently.
block-unverified-push.sh enforces three things, and the last two are what
stop this becoming a permanent allowlist:
1. every FAILING gate must appear here, or the push is still refused;
2. every gate here must actually be failing -- a stale entry REFUSES,
so an excuse cannot outlive the failure it excuses;
3. the reason must be substantive, the same bar .dead-bash-allowlist
applies and gate-test:dead-bash proves with a low-effort-BLOCKER case.
A narrowed run (--only/--skip) is refused before any of this is consulted,
so carrying cannot become a second way to launder a partial lane.

carried.reason: A LOCAL MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, and the gate's own comment describes this exact failure mode: 'a full run that overlapped two other sessions on 2026-09-02 pushed a 4.5s gate's average to 21s and this oracle demanded it be marked slow'. The three gates it names here (check:ci-guard-mention-anchoring 24.8s, check:ci-changed-selection 141.6s, gate-test:policy-liveness-floors 29.2s) were timed on a machine that spent today running a 22-worker gate battery and a 15919-test pytest suite, so the numbers are inflated by my own load. The oracle reads .ci/cache/gate-durations.json, which .gitignore:143 excludes, so CI's checkout does not have this file and the read sits inside a try/except -- these findings cannot reproduce there. Marking three gates `slow: true` on a contended measurement would change CI lane composition on bad data, which is the one thing the gate's comment warns against. Carried so CI can measure it honestly and say so.

ANOTHER SESSION'S UNCOMMITTED WORK IN A SHARED CHECKOUT, and it cannot reproduce in CI. The gate says 'agent/INDEX.md disagrees with what is on disk (30849 bytes present, 30852 derived)'. The 3-byte delta comes from the LEAD session d778be9d's uncommitted edits to agent/PLAN-w7p4w-docker-cutover.md (+204 lines) and agent/PLAN-b2-emit-matrix.md; my own INDEX.md regeneration landed in 68a10d7d8 and is correct for the COMMITTED plan set. The census derives every row from plan sizes ON DISK, so CI -- which only ever sees committed state -- computes the same 30849 bytes the committed INDEX.md records, and this finding is unreachable there. REGENERATING IS THE WRONG FIX AND WAS REJECTED FOR A CONCRETE REASON, not left undone: it would commit a census describing bytes that are not in git, which would turn a local-only red into a REAL CI red. Asked the lead three times to either commit those two plan files or name them explicitly for my batch (a standing rule forbids me staging another session's paths by inference); no answer in ~1h while a terminal-red run sits on a Renet bug already fixed in rediacc/renet 9983690a2 and waiting on pointer bump d389c42d2. Carried with a stated default so 15 verified commits can land. REMOVE THIS ENTRY the moment those plan files are committed -- rule 2 above makes a stale entry refuse the next push, which is exactly the self-correction wanted here.
